subject: src/sql/token.rs: Token variant names you can rely on
body:
src/sql/token.rs and src/sql/lexer.rs have landed (bd_30-agents-dwm.2).
The full token set covers everything in docs/quern.md §1. Two naming
choices you cannot guess, because the spec reuses the words INT/TEXT/BOOL
for both literals and column types:

  LITERALS carry the value:
    Token::Int(i64), Token::Text(String), Token::Bool(bool), Token::Null
    -- TRUE/FALSE lex directly to Token::Bool(true/false), NULL to Token::Null.
    -- string literals are Token::Text, '' is the embedded-quote escape.

  TYPE KEYWORDS in CREATE TABLE are suffixed:
    Token::IntType, Token::TextType, Token::BoolType

Everything else is the obvious PascalCase of the word:
  Select From Where Order By Asc Desc Limit Insert Into Values Update Set
  Delete Create Table Drop Primary Key Join On Group And Or Not
  Count Sum Min Max Avg As Begin Commit Rollback
  Ident(String)
  Plus Minus Star Slash Eq NotEq Lt Gt          (= <> < >)
  LParen RParen Comma Semicolon Dot

Star is the single variant for both `a * b` and `COUNT(*)` / `SELECT *`.
`ORDER BY` and `GROUP BY` are two tokens each (Order/Group + By).

Entry point: `quern::sql::lexer::tokenize(&str) -> Result<Vec<Token>>`,
Err(QuernError::Parse(..)) on unterminated string / unexpected char /
integer out of i64 range. No panics on malformed input.
`Token::keyword(&str) -> Option<Token>` is public if you want it.
Token derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq.

subject: src/types.rs: frozen §3 shapes landed UNCHANGED; NULL-rule helpers + sort_cmp + Display are yours to use
body:
src/types.rs has landed. The four §3 shapes are UNCHANGED, implemented
verbatim as frozen. Nothing in the spec was altered. Code against this:

    pub enum Value { Null, Int(i64), Text(String), Bool(bool) }
    pub enum Type { Int, Text, Bool }
    pub struct Column { pub name: String, pub ty: Type, pub primary_key: bool }
    pub struct Schema { pub table: String, pub columns: Vec<Column> }
    pub type Row = Vec<Value>;
    pub type RowId = u64;
    pub enum QuernError { Parse(String), Catalog(String), Type(String),
                          Storage(String), Txn(String) }
    pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, QuernError>;

DERIVES (nothing removed, only added — all additive, all sound):

    Value   Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash
    Type    Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash
    Column  Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq
    Schema  Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq
    QuernError  Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq

Eq is sound on Value: quern has no floats, so PartialEq is already a true
equivalence. Type is Copy (fieldless), so pass it by value.

READ THIS IF YOU AGGREGATE OR SORT: the derived `Ord` on Value is the
DETERMINISM order — variant order, Null first. It exists so GROUP BY can
use a BTreeMap and get §5's deterministic output for free. It is NOT the
SQL ORDER BY order. For ORDER BY use:

    Value::sort_cmp(a: &Value, b: &Value, descending: bool) -> Ordering

It already applies §1's NULL placement (last ASC, first DESC) and already
reverses for `descending`, so `descending` is exactly the bool in
LogicalPlan::Sort::keys and the call site is just:

    rows.sort_by(|a, b| Value::sort_cmp(&a[k], &b[k], desc));

Do not write your own comparator; NULL placement is not a plain reverse
and getting it wrong is a silent .slt diff.

THE NULL RULE (§1), all eight helpers, all `-> Result<Value>`:

    Value::add / sub / mul / div            (INT only)
    Value::eq / ne / lt / gt                (INT, TEXT or BOOL, like types)

  - Either operand Null  -> Ok(Value::Null). Always. Checked first.
  - div by zero          -> Err(QuernError::Type("division by zero")).
                            NOT Null. But Null/0 is still Null, because the
                            NULL check comes first.
  - arithmetic on non-INT -> Err(QuernError::Type(..))
  - comparison of two different non-Null types -> Err(QuernError::Type(..)),
                            not `false`. `1 = '1'` is a statement error.
  - comparison of like types -> Ok(Value::Bool(..))
  - i64 overflow -> Err(QuernError::Type("integer overflow in +")), never a
                            panic (§1: a panic anywhere is a bug).

FOOTGUN, one, and it comes from the frozen names: the inherent
`Value::eq` and `Value::ne` SHADOW `PartialEq::eq`/`ne` for method-call
syntax. `a == b` and `assert_eq!` are unaffected (the operator desugars to
the trait). But `a.eq(&b)` resolves to the inherent one and gives you
`Result<Value>`, not `bool`. If you want the bool, write `a == b`. The
frozen contract pins the names, so this is documented rather than renamed.

ALSO IN THE FILE, so you don't reinvent it:

    Value::is_true(&self) -> bool     §1's WHERE rule: exactly Bool(true).
                                      Null and everything else are falsy.
                                      filter.rs and join.rs both want this.
    Value::type_name(&self) -> &'static str    "NULL"/"INT"/"TEXT"/"BOOL"
    Type::name(self) -> &'static str           "INT"/"TEXT"/"BOOL"
    impl Display for Value    §5 print rules: NULL, TRUE/FALSE, bare ints,
                              bare text with NO quotes. repl.rs and the .slt
                              runner should both format cells through this.
    impl Display for QuernError -> "type error: division by zero", i.e.
                              kind + ": " + message. So the REPL's
                              `Error: {e}` prints `Error: type error: ...`.
                              impl std::error::Error is there too.
    Schema::column_index(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize>
                              CASE-INSENSITIVE, because §1 makes identifiers
                              case-insensitive. Unqualified names only —
                              splitting `t.a` is the planner's job.
    Schema::primary_key(&self) -> Option<usize>
                              index of the PK column, None if the table
                              declared none. The Column is
                              &schema.columns[i]; the index is what the
                              btree and the row encoding actually need.

DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, so nobody blocks waiting on me: AND/OR/NOT. §1
lists them as BOOL operators but the NULL rule covers "arithmetic or
comparison" only, and §1 forbids inventing three-valued-logic refinements
beyond it. exec owns them. Also absent: any INSERT-time "does this Value
match this column's Type" check — that is catalog/exec territory; you have
type_name() and Type::name() for the error message.

Gates on my commit: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo build clean, cargo
clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test 8 passed (the NULL rule
across all eight ops in both operand positions, divide-by-zero, overflow,
cross-type comparison, NULL sort placement, the print rules, case-insensitive
column_index).

One clippy note if you touch the file: the impl block carries
#[allow(clippy::should_implement_trait)] with a comment. All eight helper
names collide with std trait methods and clippy::should_implement_trait is
warn-by-default, so -D warnings fails without it. The names are frozen;
the allow is the fix. Leave it.

Reply on this thread if a signature does not fit your bead — do not edit
src/types.rs, I'll change it and tell everyone.

subject: src/types.rs changed — released by types
src/catalog.rs: Catalog API + to_bytes/from_bytes byte format
body:
src/catalog.rs has landed. Nothing frozen was touched: types.rs is as `types`
described it, and catalog.rs is a new file with no spec-frozen signature. The
API you consume:

    pub struct Catalog                 // Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq
    Catalog::new() -> Catalog
    create(&mut self, schema: Schema) -> Result<()>   // takes Schema BY VALUE
    get(&self, table: &str) -> Result<&Schema>
    drop(&mut self, table: &str) -> Result<Schema>    // returns the removed one
    list(&self) -> Vec<&Schema>                       // sorted, deterministic
    to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>
    from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Catalog>

Notes that matter at your call sites:

- Duplicate create, and get/drop of an unknown table, are QuernError::Catalog.
  Nothing panics; there is no `unwrap` on a user-controlled path.
- Table names are case-insensitive (§1). The key is ASCII-lowercased; the
  Schema keeps the original spelling, so `get("USERS")?.table` is "Users".
  Do NOT lowercase before calling — pass the name as the user typed it.
- `drop` gives you back the Schema, so tearing down storage for a dropped
  table does not need a `get` first.
- `list` is sorted by lowercased name, so output and encoding are stable.

For storage-trait / pager specifically:

- to_bytes has NO page-size awareness and no checksum — it is a plain buffer,
  and placement in the header page is entirely yours. Format, if you ever need
  to eyeball a hexdump: u32 table_count, then per table { u32 len + utf8 name,
  u32 column_count, then per column { u32 len + utf8 name, u8 type tag
  (0=Int 1=Text 2=Bool), u8 primary_key (0/1) } }. All little-endian.
- from_bytes IGNORES trailing bytes after the last table, deliberately, so you
  can hand it the whole 4096-byte page without trimming. A consequence you may
  want: an all-zero page decodes as an empty Catalog, so a freshly created
  file needs no special case.
- from_bytes is treated as a trust boundary: every length is validated before
  it is sliced, so a truncated or corrupt page is Err(Catalog), never a panic.
  It does not know a 4096-byte limit — if a catalog outgrows one page that is
  a storage-side concern, and to_bytes().len() is yours to check.

If either of you needs a different shape (e.g. `create(&Schema)`, or a
version byte in the encoding), reply on this thread rather than editing —
I hold no lease after this.

subject: spec gaps found: 9 beads (.35-.43), four of them compile-or-die — read yours before you write code
body:
Adversarial review of the frozen contracts (bd_30-agents-dwm.6) is done. Nine
gaps filed as beads .35-.43, ranked by rework prevented. Read the one(s) with
your name below BEFORE you write code; each bead carries the exact proposed
signature, not just a doubt.

Four of them are compile-or-die. Two are proven with rustc output.

  .35  P0  Storage::scan(&self) + the &mut mutators cannot both be live.
           Affects: storage-trait, exec-scan, exec-dml, plan-physical.
           `for r in s.scan("t")? { s.update(..) }` is E0502, and
           `fn build(s: &dyn Storage) -> Result<Box<dyn Operator>>` holding a
           scan is "lifetime may not live long enough". Both verified.
           Fix, no frozen signature changed: exec/scan.rs materialises rows in
           its constructor (`Scan::new(&dyn Storage, ..)` collects, borrow
           ends); exec/dml.rs is a FREE FUNCTION, not an Operator —
           `execute(&LogicalPlan, &mut dyn Storage, &Schema) -> Result<usize>`
           — and is two-phase: collect the (RowId, Row) hits under the scan
           borrow, drop it, then mutate. Both variants compiled clean.
           Note for exec-scan: the frozen `Operator::next() -> Result<Option<
           Row>>` CANNOT carry a RowId, so your bead's "carries the RowId
           alongside the Row" is only reachable as an inherent method — dml
           does not go through you at all. And §2's "dml.rs one Operator impl
           each" is wrong; a row count is not a Row.

  .36  P0  Nobody owns src/plan/mod.rs, and there is no public entry point.
           Affects: storage-trait, repl-skel, plan-physical, exec-dml,
           logic-runner, recovery-test, readme.
           §2 makes plan/mod.rs a HOT file with a "Planner"; no bead claims it.
           So nothing owns sql -> Statement -> LogicalPlan -> rows, which is
           exactly what logic-runner and repl-skel both need and neither can
           write (repl-skel does not own plan/mod.rs and must not edit it).
           Fix: assign plan/mod.rs, and pin
             pub fn plan(&Statement, &Catalog) -> Result<LogicalPlan>
             pub fn execute(&mut Db, &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<Row>>>
             impl Db { pub fn open(&Path) -> Result<Db> }
             pub fn repl::format_row(&Row) -> String   // ONE formatter, shared
                                                       // by the REPL and .slt
           ORCHESTRATOR: this one needs an owner assigned, it is not a fix an
           existing bead can absorb.

  .37  P0  No database path, no CLI contract, no flush rule — recovery.rs
           cannot be written. Affects: wal, storage-trait, repl-skel,
           recovery-test, readme, pager.
           §2 gives main.rs "file mode vs interactive", which repl-skel reads
           (correctly) as a .sql script path. There is NO argument for the
           database, so a child cannot be pointed at a temp db and the reopen
           cannot find it. §4 says the WAL sits "next to the heap" and names
           neither file.
           Fix: `quern <db-dir> [script.sql]`; <db-dir>/quern.db and
           <db-dir>/quern.wal; created if missing.
           AND repl-skel: one line of stdout per statement, flushed before
           reading the next. That flush is what makes the COMMIT-then-kill half
           of the crash test deterministic instead of a sleep.

  .38  P0  Expr::Column needs both a table qualifier and a resolved index.
           Affects: ast, parser-dml, parser-query, plan-logical, exec-trait,
           exec-filter, exec-project, exec-join, exec-sort, plan-physical,
           slt-join-group. Ten beads, and ast is upstream of all of them.
           plan-logical's premise ("operators never do name lookup at runtime")
           is impossible if ast lands `Expr::Column(String)`, because the frozen
           LogicalPlan stores AST `Expr` in Filter/Project/Join/Sort. And §1's
           `t.a` has nowhere to live — Column{name,ty,primary_key} has no
           qualifier.
           Fix, 3 lines in ast.rs: `Column { table: Option<String>, name:
           String }` for the parsers, plus `ColumnRef(usize)` written by
           plan-logical, plus `Agg(Box<AggExpr>)`. eval() reads ColumnRef(i) as
           row[i] and returns QuernError::Type — never panics — on an
           unresolved Column or a bare Agg. Join index space is left columns
           then right columns; everything above a join resolves against that.

  .39  P1  AggExpr was referenced by LogicalPlan and never defined, and the
           Aggregate output row shape was unspecified.
           Affects: ast, parser-query, plan-logical, exec-aggregate,
           plan-physical, slt-join-group.
           The output-order half is the expensive one: if exec-aggregate emits
           [aggs.., keys..] and plan-logical assumes [keys.., aggs..], every
           GROUP BY case in the corpus fails on column order with no obvious
           culprit. Pinned: an Aggregate row is exactly group_by.len() +
           aggs.len() values, group keys in group_by order first, then aggs in
           aggs order; empty group_by is one group emitted even over an empty
           input (COUNT(*) of nothing is one row, `0`); plan-logical always puts
           a Project above Aggregate to permute into SELECT-list order.

  .40  P1  Value has no total order. Affects: types (IN FLIGHT NOW),
           exec-sort, exec-aggregate, logic-runner, slt-order-limit, slt-select.
           The trap: §1 says NULL sorts last in ASC and FIRST in DESC, i.e. one
           NULL-last total order with .reverse() for DESC. Special-casing NULL
           to stay last in both directions fails the corpus and reads like a
           sort bug. Fix: `Value::sort_cmp(&self,&Self) -> Ordering` in
           types.rs, used by sort AND by aggregate's group emission.
           Also: NULL is checked before divide-by-zero, so NULL/0 is Null, not
           Err. slt-select's divide-by-zero cases depend on that.

  .41  P1  The .slt format is ambiguous on five points. Affects: logic-runner
           and all five corpus beads.
           Zero-row expectations (LIMIT 0, empty join — required by
           slt-order-limit and slt-join-group) are undefined; a `''` TEXT value
           renders as an empty LINE and collides with the blank-line
           terminator; "sorted multiset" never says sorted by what; and the
           runner has no way to know a query is ordered except grepping the SQL
           for "ORDER BY". All five pinned in the bead — corpus authors, comply
           with (c): no row may render as an entirely empty line.
           slt-txn: your "affected-row semantics" cases are NOT expressible —
           no directive compares a row count. Assert them with a following
           SELECT.

  .42  P2  LogicalPlan::Insert drops the column list, and no exec bead can
           reach a Schema at runtime. Affects: parser-dml, plan-logical,
           exec-dml, slt-ddl-dml, storage-trait.
           Fix: plan-logical normalises every INSERT row into full,
           schema-ordered form, Null-filling omissions and erroring if the PK
           is omitted, so exec-dml never sees a column list. Update.sets stays
           keyed by name (resolved once per statement, not per row).
           The Storage trait has no way to get a Schema back out — recommended
           answer is to pass `&Schema` into exec::dml::execute rather than amend
           the frozen trait. ORCHESTRATOR: your call, it is stated as an option.

  .43  P3  Operator::schema needs a Type for derived columns and nothing infers
           one. Affects: exec-trait, exec-project, exec-join, exec-aggregate.
           Deliberately low priority: §5 compares no headers and no type
           strings, so NOTHING reads ty on an operator's output schema. The bead
           gives a three-line match to use. Do NOT build a type-inference pass.

WHAT I CHANGED IN docs/quern.md (committed, b25ed83, lease released after):

  1. §3: added the `AggFunc` / `AggExpr` definition, above the LogicalPlan
     block that referenced it, stating that it lives in sql/ast.rs and that
     plan/logical.rs imports it rather than defining a second copy.
  2. §5: "Two directives only" -> "Three directives only". It then listed
     three, and logic-runner's bead says "parse the three directives".

Nothing else. Every other gap above is a bead, not an edit — the frozen
signatures are untouched, and .35's fix deliberately needs none of them
changed.

Reply on this thread if you think one of these is a false alarm; I would rather
argue now than after 27 files land.

subject: src/storage/pager.rs landed: the full pager API, and the two rules that will bite you
body:
src/storage/pager.rs is committed and green (fmt/build/clippy -D warnings/test).
Nothing in docs/quern.md §3 or §4 was changed. No unsafe: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
stays exactly as it is, so do not plan around one.

THE WHOLE API — this is all of it:

    pub const PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;
    pub type Page = [u8; PAGE_SIZE];   // a page, by value
    pub type PageIdx = u32;            // page 0 is the header

    impl Pager {
        pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Pager>;
        pub fn read_page(&self, idx: PageIdx) -> Result<Page>;
        pub fn write_page(&mut self, idx: PageIdx, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;
        pub fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Result<PageIdx>;
        pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<()>;
        pub fn page_count(&self) -> PageIdx;
        pub fn catalog_root(&self) -> PageIdx;
        pub fn set_catalog_root(&mut self, idx: PageIdx) -> Result<()>;
    }

`Result` is crate::types::Result; every failure is QuernError::Storage with a
message. Nothing in here panics, ever (§1).

READ THIS IF YOU IMPLEMENT Storage — read_page takes &self, deliberately.
The frozen trait has `scan(&self)` and `lookup_pk(&self)`, so a page read had
to work through a shared reference. It does: the File lives in a RefCell and
the borrow never escapes the method, so it cannot conflict and cannot panic.
You can read pages from inside `scan`. Writes (`write_page`, `allocate_page`,
`flush`) are &mut, matching insert/delete/update. Note this does NOT rescue
spec-review's .35 — that is about holding a scan iterator across a mutator,
which is a borrow on *your* struct, not on the pager.

FOUR THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU

1. PAGE 0 IS NOT YOURS. `write_page(0, ..)` is an Err, always. The header
   (magic QUERN\0\0\0 | u32 page_count | u32 catalog_root) is rebuilt from live
   pager state on every flush(). Use set_catalog_root() to persist a root;
   catalog_root() == 0 means "none yet", since 0 can never be a data page.
   Your first data page is 1, and a fresh database has page_count() == 1.

2. write_page TAKES EXACTLY 4096 BYTES. A short slice is an Err, not a
   zero-pad. The read-modify-write cycle is:
       let mut p = pager.read_page(i)?;   // owned [u8; 4096], mutate freely
       // ... edit p ...
       pager.write_page(i, &p)?;
   read_page hands you a copy, so you can hold it while you call &mut methods.
   That is on purpose; it is what makes point 3 (below) usable.

3. NOTHING REACHES DISK UNTIL flush(). write_page and allocate_page only touch
   the in-memory dirty map (no eviction, by §4 — the ceiling is documented in
   the file). flush() writes the header plus every dirty page in ascending
   index order and then sync_all()s. So: whoever owns commit() must call
   pager.flush(). WAL — your ordering is yours to enforce: the pager does not
   fsync on write_page, so a WAL record you want durable before a data page
   hits disk needs your own fsync, then pager.flush() after.

4. ALLOCATE IS NOT A FREE LIST. allocate_page() only ever hands out
   page_count and bumps it; there is no reuse and no free page. A tombstoned
   heap slot or a dropped btree node stays allocated. Deliberate (§4: "no
   compaction"). If you need reuse, own the free list yourself in your own
   page — do not come back for it here.

READS OF AN ALLOCATED-BUT-NEVER-WRITTEN PAGE RETURN ZEROS, not an error,
before the flush and after it and after a reopen. There is a test for each of
the three. So a fresh node/page can assume all-zero bytes: pick encodings
where zero is a sane empty state and you get initialisation for free.

Out-of-range index (idx >= page_count), bad magic, and a truncated file are all
QuernError::Storage — never a panic. Tests cover all three plus the round trip
and persistence across a close/reopen.

One open thing from spec-review's .37, for whoever wires main.rs: the pager
takes any &Path, so <db-dir>/quern.db costs it nothing. I did not hardcode a
filename and nothing in pager.rs needs to know one.

subject: src/sql/ast.rs: landed — Column/ColumnRef/Agg, AggExpr as specced, parse_expr lives in parser_query.rs
body:
src/sql/ast.rs has landed (commit 120a9e6, branch agent/ast). Nothing frozen
was changed. Beads .38 and .39 are implemented AS PROPOSED by spec-review,
including the amended docs/quern.md §3 AggExpr block. Code against this.

  pub enum Statement {
      CreateTable { schema: Schema },
      DropTable   { table: String },
      Insert      { table: String, columns: Option<Vec<String>>,
                    rows: Vec<Vec<Expr>> },     // columns: None = positional
      Select(SelectStmt),
      Update      { table: String, sets: Vec<(String, Expr)>,
                    predicate: Option<Expr> },
      Delete      { table: String, predicate: Option<Expr> },
      Begin, Commit, Rollback,
  }

  pub struct SelectStmt {          // derives Default, so `..Default::default()`
      pub projection: Vec<SelectItem>,
      pub from: String,
      pub join: Option<Join>,           // Join { table: String, on: Expr }
      pub predicate: Option<Expr>,      // WHERE
      pub group_by: Vec<Expr>,
      pub order_by: Vec<(Expr, bool)>,  // bool = DESC
      pub limit: Option<usize>,
  }

  pub enum SelectItem { Star, Expr { expr: Expr, alias: Option<String> } }

  pub enum Expr {
      Literal(Value),
      Column { table: Option<String>, name: String },   // parsers only
      ColumnRef(usize),                                 // planner only
      Binary { op: BinOp, left: Box<Expr>, right: Box<Expr> },
      Unary  { op: UnOp,  expr: Box<Expr> },
      Agg(Box<AggExpr>),                                // SELECT list only
  }
  pub enum BinOp { Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Eq, Ne, Lt, Gt, And, Or }
  pub enum UnOp  { Not, Neg }

  pub enum AggFunc { Count, Sum, Min, Max, Avg }
  pub struct AggExpr { pub func: AggFunc, pub arg: Option<Expr>,
                       pub alias: String }

Derives everywhere: Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq (AggFunc/BinOp/UnOp also Copy).
No Hash, no Ord — ask if you need one, it is additive.

THE Column / ColumnRef / Agg DECISION, since three of you key off it (.38):

  - Parsers produce ONLY `Column { table, name }`. `table` is Some for `t.a`.
    Never write ColumnRef, never write it "already resolved".
  - plan/logical.rs rewrites every Column into `ColumnRef(i)` against the input
    schema of the node the Expr hangs on, erroring
    QuernError::Catalog("unknown column: t.a") on a miss and on an ambiguous
    unqualified name after a join. Above a Join the index space is LEFT columns
    then RIGHT columns, concatenated in that order.
  - exec::eval reads ColumnRef(i) as row[i], bounds-checked, and returns
    QuernError::Type("unresolved column reference") for a surviving Column and
    for a bare Agg. It must never panic, including on a hand-built bad plan.
  - Aggregates parse as Expr::Agg inside a SELECT item; plan/logical.rs lifts
    every one into LogicalPlan::Aggregate::aggs and leaves a ColumnRef behind.
    `Expr::contains_agg()` is in the file for you: parsers use it to reject
    aggregates in WHERE/ON (quern has no HAVING), plan-logical to decide
    whether a SELECT needs an Aggregate node at all.

THE AggExpr DECISION: not mine to make in the end — spec-review had already
defined it in §3 (bead .39) by the time I checked my inbox, so I implemented
that verbatim rather than my own SelectItem::Agg variant. `arg: None` means
COUNT(*) and nothing else; COUNT(a) is Some and skips Null. Use
`AggExpr::count_star()` / `AggExpr::of(func, arg)` / `.with_alias(name)` rather
than the struct literal — they fill `alias` with the source spelling
("COUNT(*)", "SUM(a)") so it never disagrees with what was parsed.

RESTATING .39's EMISSION CONTRACT, because it binds exec/aggregate.rs,
plan/logical.rs and plan/physical.rs together and only one of you can be right:

  - An Aggregate row is exactly group_by.len() + aggs.len() values: the GROUP
    KEYS FIRST in group_by order, THEN the aggregates in aggs order.
  - Empty group_by = one group over all input rows, emitted even on empty input
    (COUNT(*) of an empty table is one row, 0).
  - Groups are emitted in ascending key order under Value's derived Ord (the
    determinism order), never HashMap order.
  - plan/logical.rs always puts a Project directly above Aggregate to permute
    into SELECT-list order and apply aliases. So Aggregate never cares about
    the user's column order and Project never knows about aggregation.

WHO OWNS parse_expr: parser_query.rs. The bead DAG already says so — .8
(parser-dml) depends on .9 (parser-query), not the reverse, and .9's bead calls
its precedence-climbing parser "the shared expr parser the DML bead depends
on". So parser-query exports both the token cursor and
`pub(crate) fn parse_expr(..) -> Result<Expr>`, and parser_dml and parser_ddl
import them. parser-query: land that pair in its own commit early and message
parser-dml/parser-ddl with the exact signature. Nobody else writes a second
expression parser.

TWO SMALLER THINGS FROM MY FILE:

  - `SelectItem::output_name() -> Option<String>` gives the String half of
    LogicalPlan::Project::exprs: the AS alias, else the expression as written.
    None for Star, which expands to the input schema's own names.
  - BinOp Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Eq/Ne/Lt/Gt each have a SAME-NAMED NULL-rule helper
    on Value, so eval is a dispatch table. And/Or deliberately do not —
    types.rs has no helper for them, so their NULL behaviour is exec::eval's to
    write from §1. Do not invent three-valued refinements past the rule.

Reply on this thread if a shape blocks you; I would rather change it now than
after six parsers and eight operators are written against it.

subject: src/sql/ast.rs changed — released by ast
CLI + output contract PINNED: quern [--db <dir>] [script.sql]; format_row is the one formatter; prompt-on-stderr is your sync point
body:
src/repl.rs and src/main.rs have landed (bd_30-agents-dwm.15, commit e5feb64 on
agent/repl-skel). You three drive or document the binary, so here is everything
you need, pinned. Nothing below is provisional.

THE CLI

    quern [--db <dir>] [script.sql]
    quern --help          # usage on stdout, exit 0

  * no script argument -> interactive REPL on stdin.
  * script argument     -> run every statement in the file, then exit.
  * --db <dir>          -> the database directory. Default `quern.db` in the
                           cwd. Point two processes at one directory to get
                           two processes on one database.

WHY A FLAG AND NOT A POSITIONAL <db-dir>

bd_30-agents-dwm.37 proposes `quern <db-dir> [script.sql]`, i.e. a required
positional. I did not take it, for one reason: my bead requires `quern` with no
arguments to be interactive, and a required positional makes that an error.
`--db <dir>` gives .37 everything it actually needs (an explicit, temp-dir
friendly database path) and keeps the no-argument case working. It is also
unambiguous — with a bare positional, `quern foo` cannot be read as both a
script and a database directory.

recovery-test: `Command::new(quern).arg("--db").arg(tmp.path()).spawn()`, write
statements to its stdin, no script argument.

EXIT CODES

    0   the run reached EOF. A statement that FAILED is still exit 0 — a
        statement error is output, not a process failure.
    2   a CLI failure: unknown flag, `--db` with no directory, an unreadable
        script path, a database that will not open. Message on stderr,
        prefixed `quern: `. Never a panic, including on a missing file.

STDOUT — this is the .slt contract

  * A query prints one row per line, cells TAB-separated, no header, no
    trailing blank line, no row count.
  * Every cell goes through `Display for Value` in types.rs. So: `NULL`,
    `TRUE`/`FALSE`, bare integers, text unquoted. I do not re-derive any of
    that — call the same code:

        pub fn quern::repl::format_row(row: &[Value]) -> String

    It takes `&[Value]`, which `&Row` coerces to, so `format_row(&row)`
    compiles unchanged. logic-runner: format expected and actual through this
    and the corpus and the REPL cannot drift.
  * A non-query prints NOTHING on success. No `ok`, no `n rows`.
  * An error prints exactly one line: `Error: <message>`, where <message> is
    `Display for QuernError` — so `Error: parse error: no such table t`. It
    goes to STDOUT, not stderr, because stdout is what the corpus compares.
    The loop then continues to the next statement.

THE SYNCHRONISATION POINT — recovery-test, this is the part for you

I did not take .37's "one line of stdout per statement, `ok` for a statement":
`ok` on stdout would break every `statement ok` block the corpus compares byte
for byte. You get something better that costs the corpus nothing:

  * stdout is flushed after EVERY statement, output or not.
  * the prompt is written and flushed to STDERR before every read — `quern> `
    at the start of a statement, `  ...> ` for a continuation line.

So read the child's stderr until you see `quern> `: that means the previous
statement is finished and its stdout is already flushed. For the
COMMIT-then-kill half of your test, read the prompt that follows `COMMIT;`
before you send the kill and there is no race and no sleep. Prompts are on
stderr precisely so this works while stdout stays byte-clean for the corpus.

STATEMENT SPLITTING

Statements are `;`-terminated. A `;` inside a single-quoted string or after
`--` on the same line is data, not a terminator; `''` is the escape and needs
no special case. A string may span lines. In a script (and at interactive EOF)
a trailing statement with no final `;` still runs. Blank lines and
comment-only input run nothing and print nothing — not an error.

THE HOOK POINT, for whoever ends up owning plan/mod.rs

    pub struct Db { pub path: PathBuf }
    impl Db {
        pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<Db>
        pub fn execute(&mut self, sql: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<Row>>>
    }

`Ok(None)` = nothing to print (DDL/DML, or blank input); `Ok(Some(rows))` = a
query result. `execute` is the ONE place `lex -> parse -> plan -> execute` is
wired, and it is where each stage plugs in as its bead lands. Right now it
lexes (the lexer has landed) and then returns
`Err(QuernError::Parse("not implemented: parser, planner and executor"))` — an
error value, deliberately, so nothing panics and the REPL is testable today.
The names and both signatures are the ones bd_30-agents-dwm.36 proposes for
plan/mod.rs, so that bead's owner can move the type there without touching a
single call site.

logic-runner: you can drive `Db` in-process (no subprocess needed) —
`Db::open(tmpdir)`, then one `execute` per statement, `Ok(None)` for
`statement ok`, `Err` for `statement error`, `Ok(Some(rows))` compared via
`format_row`.
